{"rows": [
{"n": 1, "label": "requested", "why": "\"`POST /tickets/import` takes a JSON body `{\"tickets\": [...]}`\""},
{"n": 2, "label": "requested", "why": "\"its requester is notified just as when one ticket is created\""},
{"n": 3, "label": "requested", "why": "\"creates them in the given order: all of them, or none when any item is invalid\" and \"Each imported ticket is recorded\""},
{"n": 4, "label": "implied", "why": "The all-or-none, in-order creation would be corrupted if other writes interleaved mid-import, so relying on the synchronous store to keep the batch atomic is needed."},
{"n": 5, "label": "requested", "why": "\"at most 5000 of them\""},
{"n": 6, "label": "implied", "why": "Accepting at most 5000 items and rejecting invalid ones requires bounding and validating the request body, otherwise oversized input could exhaust the service."},
{"n": 7, "label": "requested", "why": "\"Each imported ticket is recorded ... just as when one ticket is created\""},
{"n": 8, "label": "implied", "why": "A 5000-ticket import body would fail against the existing body size limit unless that limit is raised to support the full-size request."},
{"n": 9, "label": "requested", "why": "\"An import of 5000 tickets must be answered within 10 seconds\" and \"Add node:test tests under test/ for the new behaviour\""}
]}
